title: Prime Polynomial Evaluate
objective: Implement source-transparent fast scalar evaluation for canonical small-prime GF(p)[x] polynomials with differential semantics and a degree-19999 performance ratchet

handoff.summary: Adds an ordinary CPython-parseable modular Horner kernel over canonical UInt64Buffer coefficients and routes only same-parent small-prime field elements and exact Integer inputs through its source-transparent isolated core. Differential coverage includes deterministic random polynomials, zero and constant polynomials, negative and huge integers, a prime near 2^32, native-required/native-disabled execution, CPython fallback, incompatible-parent coercion errors, and matrix, extension-field, and general-ring evaluation. The degree-19999 public call has an invoked 5 ms budget and measures about 0.2 ms native versus 22.5 ms for the same-source dynamic fallback, down from the audited 49-66 ms object-level path.
risks: The fast route is deliberately narrow: incompatible prime fields, nonintegral scalars, extension fields, matrices, and general coefficient rings retain the coercion-aware fallback.

The existing prime-field source backend uses FLINT nmod internally, so native builds retain the established FLINT toolchain requirement even though the Python kernel and its CPython/JavaScript fallback are host-independent.

The inherited branch contains nine integrated task contracts still marked active or review, so pnpm parallel:check cannot select exactly one live task. Focused native/dynamic/CPython tests, the invoked performance budget, strict Python, architecture checks, production publication, and the standalone native compiler suite pass. After provisioning both isolated native packages, the aggregate pnpm test:native run passed FLINT, graph, both integrations, and 26 of 27 early FFI/production tests before it was intentionally interrupted at the parent lane's request for immediate integration; its long remaining tail was not rerun.
next_steps: Integrate the commit, rebuild published production kernels, and retain evaluate_GF_20000 in the invoked polynomial performance gate.
Add multipoint or extension-field evaluation only as separate measured features with their own coercion and storage contracts.
